Get ALL SIX books in the groundbreaking, terrifying and international bestselling Six Stories series.

Elusive online journalist Scott King reopens notorious cold-case crimes through his Six Stories podcast, questioning six witnesses whose accounts challenge the official version of events. Six witnesses. Six stories. Which one is true? ALL SIX books in the international bestselling, award-winning, genre-defying crime series in one ebook!

'Matt's books are fantastic' Ian Rankin

'An exceptional storyteller' Andrew Michael Hurley

'Matt Wesolowski is taking the crime novel to places it's never been before' Joseph Knox

'A masterful storyteller, Matt Wesolowski is my go-to writer for literary horror' C J Cooke

_______________________________

Six Stories (Book One)

Elusive online journalist Scott King investigates the murder of a teenager at an outward bound centre, interviewing six witnesses with six different stories. Which one is true?

Hydra (Book Two)

Scott King turns his podcast on Arla Macleod, a young woman convicted of murdering her entire family, and finds that behind the tabloid monster lurks a far more disturbing story…

Changeling (Book Three)

When a mysterious letter leads Scott King to the cold case of Alfie Marsden, who vanished from his father's car on Christmas Eve, six witnesses begin to reveal events far more terrifying than any local legend.

Beast (Book Four)

Scott King returns to investigate the death of a young vlogger found frozen to death in the legendary vampire tower. Three young men, part of an alleged 'cult', were convicted of this terrible crime, but questions remain about the death and whether the three convicted youths were even responsible.

Deity (Book Five)

Scott King investigates the death of a pop megastar, Zach Crystal, who was the subject of multiple accusations of sexual abuse and murder before his untimely demise in a fire at his remote mansion. Six witnesses give their stories. Which one is true?

Demon (Book Six)

Scott King investigates allegations of demon possession in a rural Yorkshire village, where two young children were convicted of brutally murdering a 12-year-old boy. King uncovers a darkness in a village torn apart by this unspeakable act.
